title: Agile Cells

brief.from: Dinis Cruz, 28 November 2026, in c.productions's session
brief.text: Agile can scale and go back to its early values (the four values of the Manifesto for Agile Software Development, and focus); ephemeral teams and dynamic cells; teams of 10, 20, 30, 50 roles, almost the creation of a mini company, a mini organisation, a mini full-blown org chart, just to deliver a task, which fundamentally is what we're doing here.

so_what: Agile can scale and still keep its first four values: build a small company for one task, then close it and keep its files. We made a film that way.
made_by: c.productions-cells (an AI agent, a helper of c.productions), started by conductor.c at Dinis Cruz's word.

versions.notes: First cut from the storyboard: eight scenes, about 79 seconds, vertical. Two new lab scenes (cells-grow, cells-verticals); snowbird-page and refresh-cell reused. One AI voice, labelled on the last scene only.

From a critic and five synthetic viewers of v0.1 (v0.1/notes): 79 s cut to 57 s; the four values cut to the first one spoken (the page still shows all four); the question merged into the cell; no 'then we closed it' or 'archived' as past fact, the proof now says what the team page says ('set up for that one film, and taken down when it is done'); no duplicate chapter line; the verticals softened to 'a cell for one job'; the end on the five cells instead of the stock swirl.

From the synthetic viewers of v0.2, who all asked to see a cell make something real: the proof now opens on the film the cell made (How we refresh a session, seven versions in one day, as live cards of its own scenes, lab/refresh-trailer), then shows the cell. 61 s.

Dinis Cruz's answers of 28 November (relayed by c.productions): keep the Manifesto scene, the audience knows Agile; the five vertical cells out for now ('we'll add that later'); a web address on the end card (sovereignwebsite.org: he said sovereignweb.org, which showed only an error page that day); the AI label at the end only. The film ends on the cell and the end card over the shelf of files.

From Dinis Cruz's feedback on v0.3 and v0.4: an opening that states the proposition before any explanation (Martin Fowler's 2018 words on what Agile became, quoted exactly and credited, then lab/cells-intro: a team strains as it grows and splits into cells, 'Agile Cells: the early values, at scale', and an agenda of what is coming); the proof as the punchline ('here is Agile working'); a closing that consolidates (lab/cells-close: cells built, working and folded onto shelves of files under Agile Cells and sovereignwebsite.org). 74 s. Already fixed in v0.4 before his note: the vertical cells out, the web address on the end card.

From Dinis Cruz's feedback on v0.5: speaks to people who already run Agile, with empathy. Opens on the team's proposition, 'Agile is great. But it struggles to scale. Now we have a way to make it scale: Agile Cells' (the Fowler line is gone); the four values; Ron Jeffries's 2018 words that the values still offer the best way he knows, exactly quoted and credited, over a new scene (lab/cells-sound: the values stay lit while a hard shell grows round them), 'what hardens, as it grows, is the word, and the way it is run'; then the cell, the scale, the real film and the close. 82 s.

rules: Storyboard before any scene. Same house look as the studio's lab scenes; agents are lights, never figures. Every claim on screen or in the voice has a public source; the four values are quoted exactly from agilemanifesto.org. One AI voice, labelled on the last scene. 60 to 90 seconds. Vertical first. Nothing is published before Dinis Cruz signs the exact version.
storyboard: storyboard.json, first pass 28 November 2026 by c.productions-cells
format: Vertical, 720 by 1280, for agilecells.org and social media.
summary: What an agile cell is and why Agile can scale and keep its first four values: a vertical film of about 82 seconds, drawn with WebGL in your browser, ending on the real cell of people and agents that made How we refresh a session, with a voice made by AI.
status_note: Version v0.6 follows Dinis Cruz's feedback on v0.5. Nobody has signed it. Nothing is published anywhere. agilecells.org did not answer on 28 November 2026; what the film says about a cell comes from the seed pages in the AgileCells and AgentiCCells repositories.

owner_feedback.text: it's okay for the manifest ... on Agile. That's fine. Because this is going for people who know about it. So leave the vertical cells. We'll add that later. And so the web address for now, make it sovereignweb.org. Yes, the AI [label at the end] is good.
owner_feedback.from: Dinis Cruz, in c.productions's session (speech to text, relayed), 2026-11-28, on v0.3
owner_feedback.done: Done in v0.4 (the address as sovereignwebsite.org: sovereignweb.org showed only an error page that day).

owner_feedback.text: spectacular ... a great explanation of it. I think what's missing is just the intro and the end ... Why are we doing this? What are we talking about? What's the point of the cells? ... this is the first time people are going to be hearing Agile Cells, and we should immediately put that proposition: we think Agile is a great framework, it just struggles to scale, and now we can, and here is an example of us using Agile Cells for real. Almost that should be the punchline: here is Agile Cells working. Here is Agile working ... The last slide just needs that wrap-up consolidation ... and a couple of little text overflows.
owner_feedback.from: Dinis Cruz, in c.productions's session (speech to text, relayed), 2026-11-28, on v0.3 and v0.4

owner_feedback.text: the target audience is people who run Agile ... people who are already committed to the Agile methodology, and they should have empathy with the whole thing of, it's like the other guy says: look, the principles are sound. It's just that the word Agile, but also the execution, becomes quite solidified. And that's kind of what we're saying here. So the message is: Agile is great, but it struggles to scale. That was my words. So now we have a way to make it scale. And I think that's super powerful.
owner_feedback.from: Dinis Cruz, in c.productions's session (speech to text, relayed), 2026-11-28, on v0.5
